title: Scalar adjunction and restriction transport for the field presentation
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. Work on sites small in compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\underline G(P)=C(P,G)$ for profinite $P$, and $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ over finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. For a commutative condensed ring $R$ put $R_T=p_T^*R$, use internal module categories and ordinary unbounded derived categories, and write $\mathcal A_G(R)$ for internal $R$-modules with $\underline G$-action [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Suppose given a ringed-topos equivalence over the condensed topos whose induced exact additive module equivalences $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}\simeq\mathcal A_G(R)$ have the normalized formula $(E_RN)(P)=N(\bar s[P])$, naturally in $P$ and in $R$. For every map $\varphi:R\to R'$ these equivalences admit scalar data of [def-sfb-field-action-scalar-transport-data]. In detail the comparison $E_R\operatorname{Res}_s\cong\operatorname{Res}_G E_{R'}$ is the identity on sections: restriction changes only the scalar action via $\varphi_P$. Ordinary scalar extension is identified by this comparison and its left-adjoint comparison, preserving all Hom transposes, units and counits [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The local transposition is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and evaluation is $r'\otimes m\mapsto r'f(m)$, also after module sheafification. The tensor and tensor-unit comparisons are the balanced pure-tensor comparison and the identity on the regular module.

Writing $S_T=R'_T\otimes^L_{R_T}-$ and $S_G=R'\otimes^L_R-$ in the action categories, the induced comparison $D(E_{R'})S_s\cong S_GD(E_R)$ is obtained by applying this same tensor comparison to K-flat representatives. Ringed equivalence preserves K-flatness in both directions: its tensor comparison and exact inverse identify tensor with each acyclic complex. Derived scalar extension is the K-flat derived pullback along the identity-topos coefficient morphism, left adjoint to exact scalar restriction. Both derived adjunction bijections are localizations of the same chain-level transposition; the field comparison and the forgotten-module comparison therefore preserve the derived units and counits, with the total-left-derived counit and shift normalization in the cited scalar-data definition. This holds for arbitrary non-flat $\varphi$.

Moreover, for every qcqs $k$-scheme $X$ with structure morphism $a:X\to s$, the canonical comparison
$$\rho_a:Ra_{*,R}\operatorname{Res}_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_sRa_{*,R'}$$
is the direct-image composition comparison for the two factorizations of the identical composite ringed-topos morphism, with scalar restriction viewed as direct image on the identity topos. Its normalization is the K-injective resolution comparison, equivalently the total-right-derived-unit comparison, and its ordinary comparison is identity on the underlying sections [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For the total derived geometric section functors $\mathcal K_R$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent], the analogous normalized comparison $\mathcal K_R\operatorname{Res}_X\cong\operatorname{Res}_G\mathcal K_{R'}$ is the transport of $\rho_a$ through the ordinary identity on geometric sections. These specify a single comparison, rather than an arbitrary automorphism of isomorphic derived objects.

proof.text: Use the action-site presentation to regard $\mathcal A_G(R)$ as modules over the trivially acted-on ring on a small topos. The internal/section-ring equivalence preserves scalar restriction and extension, including their adjunctions. In the given field presentation, restricting an $R'$-module changes $r\cdot m$ to $\varphi_P(r)m$ and changes neither sections nor restriction or action maps. Thus $b:E_R\operatorname{Res}_s\cong\operatorname{Res}_G E_{R'}$ has identity components in the normalized coordinates. Restriction is exact by the scalar adjunction package. Forgetting the action is the exact module inverse image associated to restriction from $\underline G$ to the trivial group, with its specified ring identification. These identifications supply small ringed-site presentations for all the scalar and forgetting comparisons used below.

source.place: Identity-topos coefficient morphisms; sites-modules.tex Tags 03CU and 03CZ (tensor/restriction adjunctions)

proof.text: The ordinary adjunction has forward formula $h\mapsto(m\mapsto h(1\otimes m))$ and inverse $f\mapsto(r'\otimes m\mapsto r'f(m))$. The latter is balanced because $r'\varphi(r)f(m)=r'f(rm)$; both formulas commute with restrictions and the $G$-action. Their two composites are identities on pure tensors and on $m$. Module sheafification extends these maps uniquely, so the formulas remain inverse on sheaves. The given equivalence is the module pullback $e^*$ of a ringed-topos equivalence $e$, and $e^*$ has the canonical natural tensor comparison $e^*(M\otimes N)\cong e^*M\otimes e^*N$ of the ringed module-pullback tensor theorem; its inverse has the inverse comparison. The equivalence and its inverse preserve colimits. For $h=e$ with $A=R_s\to B=R'_s$, the scalar comparison theorem gives the invertible coequalizer comparison $\chi_e$ preserving $p\mapsto1\otimes p$. Applying these comparisons to the two balancing arrows in the relative tensor coequalizer therefore gives inverse tensor comparisons, determined by these generators; the regular-module comparison is the given ring comparison, hence identity in normalized coordinates. For scalar extension this gives $E_{R'}\operatorname{Ext}_s\cong\operatorname{Ext}_G E_R$. Under $b$, both adjunction transposes send $h$ to $h(1\otimes -)$, so every Hom transpose agrees. Taking $h$ or its transpose to be an identity proves the asserted unit and counit equations, including after forgetting action.

Let $E=E_R$ and let $V$ be its exact inverse. The module-pullback tensor comparison of step 2 for $e$, and its inverse for the inverse equivalence, extends to total complexes: equivalences preserve the coproducts in each total degree. If $P$ is K-flat and $A$ is an acyclic complex on the action side, $VA$ is acyclic and
$$A\otimes_R EP\cong E(VA\otimes_{R_s}P)$$
is acyclic. This is exactly the K-flat test. Apply the same argument to $V$ for the converse. The degree-zero version with short exact sequences shows preservation of flat terms. Thus $E$ and $V$ carry flat-term K-flat resolutions to such resolutions; this agrees with the ringed pullback K-flatness theorem applied to $e$ and to its inverse, whose structural ring maps are isomorphisms, so $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M\cong u^{-1}M$ by $s\otimes m\mapsto sm$. The resolving-class localization identifies these representatives with the entire unbounded derived category; no boundedness or coefficient flatness enters this argument.

proof.text:
Apply the sheaf-ring coefficient-adjunction theorem on the field, action, and underlying condensed sites. For the identity-topos morphism with ring map $R\to R'$, its pullback is ordinary scalar extension and its direct image is exact restriction. Its derived pullback is computed on flat-term K-flat resolutions and has its universal computation counit; its adjunction to termwise restriction has the chain formulas of step 2. The internal/section-ring comparisons identify these with the internal scalar functors. Since $E_R$ is an exact inverse image and $E_R(R_s')=R'$ naturally in coefficients, the scalar comparison theorem for inverse images applies: on a resolution $P$, the comparison
$$D(E_{R'})S_s(QP)\cong S_GD(E_R)(QP)$$
is the localization of the ordinary balanced comparison in step 2. Step 3 verifies that both sides are computed on these same resolutions. The scalar comparison theorem identifies this map with the adjunction mate of $D(b)$, so it preserves the actual derived adjunction, rather than merely identifying the two objects. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary ring maps.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 07A6; derived.tex Tags 0FND and 09T5; inverse-image scalar comparison via Tag 03EL

proof.text: Apply the same inverse-image scalar comparison theorem to the action-forgetting morphism of step 1. It identifies the forgotten scalar-extension comparison with the mate of its literal underlying-module restriction comparison. In both the field and forgetting squares, equality of all Hom transposes follows from that mate equation. In particular the derived units are the transposes of identity maps, and the derived counits are inverse transposes of identity maps. On representatives these are respectively $p\mapsto1\otimes p$ and $r'\otimes p\mapsto r'g(p)$ for a resolution map $g:P\to\operatorname{Res}N$; hence they have the specified total-derived normalization. For shifts, termwise restriction has the identity signed comparison. The chain formulas commute with $[n]$: the differential on each shifted complex is $(-1)^n d$, and all maps are additive of degree zero. The left-adjoint shift is characterized by transposition against this fixed restriction shift. Consequently the two mate comparisons preserve that shift and both adjunction maps, exactly as required by the scalar-data definition.

For $T=X,s$, let $i_T:(T,R'_T)\to(T,R_T)$ be the identity-topos coefficient morphism. The definition $p_X^*=\pi_X^*p^*$ and $\pi_s a=\pi_X$ give $a^{-1}p_s^*\cong p_X^*$ naturally in the coefficient ring, hence the identical composite $a_Ri_X=i_sa_{R'}$. Underived direct images on both sides are the same sections, with the action restricted via $\varphi$. Let $\kappa$ be the canonical right-derived composition isomorphism. Define
$$\rho_a=\kappa_{i_s,a_{R'}}\circ\kappa_{a_R,i_X}^{-1}:
Ra_{*,R}\,D(\operatorname{Res}_X)\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Res}_s)Ra_{*,R'}.$$
Here the exact-functor identification replaces $Ri_{T*}$ by $D(\operatorname{Res}_T)$. The composition theorem supplies invertibility and the precise K-injective resolution formula. Its computation-unit normalization is inherited from the two total right derived composition maps. Compatibility of these compositors with the canonical adjunctions is the ringed derived comparison theorem. This proves the requested normalization without assuming that scalar restriction carries K-injectives to K-injectives.

Write $F_R=E_Ra_{*,R}$. The geometric-section identification gives $(F_RM)(P)=\Gamma(X^s[P],M|_{X^s[P]})$, with its actual scalar and $G$-actions. The exact equivalence $E_R$ and its inverse preserve K-injectives; thus its right derived functor is $D(E_R)$, and the normalized composition comparison identifies $\mathcal K_R=RF_R$ with $D(E_R)Ra_{*,R}$. Conjugate $\rho_a$ by these comparisons and then by $D(b)$. The resulting isomorphism is
$$\mathcal K_R\operatorname{Res}_X\cong\operatorname{Res}_G\mathcal K_{R'}.$$
Before deriving, each factor is identity on $\Gamma(X^s[P],M|_{X^s[P]})$, so its composite is the ordinary geometric-section scalar comparison. The canonical composition and exact-equivalence identifications retain their computation units; composing their equations proves the required total-right-derived-unit equation for this composite. Uniqueness in the total derived universal property fixes it. Together with steps 1--5 this provides the scalar data and all the asserted normalized comparisons.
